title: Launch a PS2 image with spaces or a leading dash in its filename
summary: Use PCSX2’s `--` delimiter so the remaining command-line text is treated as the boot filename, including spaces or a leading dash.
heroAlt: Reflective data side of a PlayStation 2 DVD in its disc tray.
author: EmuCore - Hub
searchKeywords: Launch a PS2 image with spaces or a leading dash in its filename

blocks.text: PCSX2 documents the command pattern `pcsx2-qt.exe [parameters] [--] [boot filename]` and states that `--` is useful when the filename contains spaces or begins with a dash. After the delimiter, PCSX2 treats the remaining command-line text as the boot filename rather than parsing it as more options. The shell still needs to locate the executable; quote the executable path according to your shell if that path itself contains spaces.

Use PCSX2 from the official project and a game image you made from a disc you own or are authorized to use. Record the exact filename and keep the image unchanged during the test. Quote the executable path for your shell if needed; after `--`, use PCSX2’s documented filename handling rather than adding shell-specific quoting around the image path unless your shell requires it.

items: 1. Locate `pcsx2-qt.exe` and the full path of your lawful PS2 image.
2. Open a terminal in the executable folder or copy your known-good launcher.
3. Place any PCSX2 switches before `--`; omit optional switches for the first test.
4. Add `--` followed by the complete boot filename. PCSX2 documents that text after the delimiter is treated as the filename, so spaces and an initial dash are allowed there.
5. Start the command and wait for PCSX2 to boot the image.
6. Confirm the title matches the intended image, then stop at a safe menu.

blocks.text: The check passes when PCSX2 opens the intended image whose filename contains spaces or starts with a dash. Confirm the title and stop at its menu. This verifies argument parsing only; it does not validate image integrity or game compatibility.

items: Executable path is not recognized: quote its path using the terminal’s rules or run the command from its directory.
PCSX2 cannot locate the image: verify the complete filename after `--` and the directory path.
PCSX2 reports an unknown option: place `--` before the filename so its leading dash is not parsed as a switch.
A different title boots: check the exact filename after `--`.

blocks.text: Close PCSX2 normally and remove the temporary command or shortcut. No emulator data needs to be reset. Preserve the image filename if other library records use it.
